content.comment_body: Hello, can anyone assist? I'm trying to use a softkey in my diagram, but the outcome is always incorrect. Image 01 shows part of my diagram; image 02 shows the message text configuration; image 03 displays the result; and image 04 shows the resource usage of [product_name] [version_no]. Why does the B325 softkey block display as “?N7”? What does this indicate? Thank you for any help.

Hello, in your setup, the softkey will function only if you activate I3 first. The software key needs a HIGH or LOW signal before it, and if you then set the softkey to "ON", it switches the signal ahead of it. You might want to check my example to gain more experience. Hope this helps.

Issues can arise in the [product_name] software when block numbers exceed 200. To resolve this, you can replace a simple block such as AND or OR with one that has a lower number—just replace, don't remove it. This frees the lower number. Then, delete the B325 block and add a new softkey block, which will use the now available small number.

Yes, that worked! Thank you—you're truly knowledgeable. Is this your own discovery, or is it commonly known that block numbers above 200 can cause problems? I don't recall seeing this mentioned in the [product_name] manual.
This isn't in the official documentation, but it's discussed in technical forums related to [company_name]. There are posts about this in both the German and English sections.

Hello, the issue with block numbering was present when [product_name] [version_no] was first released. I've used [product_name] [version_no] since the start and haven't encountered this issue with newer versions.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered unexpected behavior with the softkey functionality in their diagrams, which seemed to be linked to using blocks numbered above 200. This issue was not mentioned in official documentation, but was known within technical communities. While the problem appears less common in newer versions, users resorted to workarounds, like reassigning lower block numbers to resolve it. This highlights some undocumented system limitations and instability in earlier releases.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect softkey blocks to operate reliably regardless of block numbering, and desire clear documentation regarding any limitations.
